name: Dusty Grey
lede: Dusty Grey is a middle, nearly neutral grey, built by putting the modifier dusty in front of the base color grey rather than naming anything in particular.

sections.title: A modifier on grey
sections.body:
Dusty Grey puts the modifier word dusty in front of the base color [[grey]], in the compound-modifier grammar ColorHub's library uses for descriptive names like this one [1]. Ridgway's 1912 *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature* carries a close swatch on plate LII, hue 59'''', an aged plate scan read as approximate; the RAL system of 1927 later filed near matches too, RAL 7037 and RAL 9023, themselves screen approximations [1].

Its nearest named neighbor is [[battleship-grey]], 2.6 units off, close enough to read as the same grey on screen [1]; [[deep-plumbeous]] sits 4.2 off and [[nickel]] 4.4 [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive finds a color within six units of this swatch in 524 of 23,781 paintings, 2.2 percent, as photographed; looking inside each painting for at least five percent coverage narrows that to 268 [2]. That makes it more common than 75 percent of the named colors in our library [2]. It peaks in the 1900s, present in 2.0 percent of our 1,674 paintings from that decade, 1.5 times the museums' baseline rate [2]. Inside a painting it most often sits as a mid-tone, in 39 percent of its 268 appearances by lightness rank [2].

Philips Wouwerman is its most devoted painter on file, present in 6 of his 36 works here, more than seven times the baseline rate for the museums that hold them [2]. The earliest match dates to 1278, more than six centuries before the name's 1912 record, so it marks a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not a surviving pigment [2]. It shares canvases with [[blackish-slate|Blackish Grey]] and Dark Grey more often than chance [2].
